sop_modules.name: Trim Prime Setup
sop_modules.description: Floor protection and staging for trim priming. Wall masking and fixture covers only required for spray application method.

tasks.name: Setup Floor Protection
tasks.description: Lay drop cloth runners along baseboard and trim work areas to catch drips. Position perimeter drops under work zones.

quality_notes.all: Drops positioned to catch drips from trim work. Edges secured.

tasks.name: Mask Wall at Trim Edge
tasks.description: Apply tape and masking paper to wall surface at trim edge to protect from spray overspray. Required for spray application only.

quality_notes.all: Tape applied at trim-wall junction. Paper extends 12 inches minimum to catch overspray.

tasks.name: Cover Fixtures Near Spray Zone
tasks.description: Apply covers to electrical outlets and switches adjacent to trim work area. Required for spray application only.

quality_notes.all: All outlets and switches within spray zone covered.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Floor protection first, then wall masking (spray only), then fixture covers (spray only). Setup must complete before any prep work begins.

sop_modules.name: Trim Initial Prep
sop_modules.description: Surface preparation before primer coat: dust wipe, fill fasteners, fill end grain, caulk joints, and sand. Per Fine_Finish_Doctrine Section 6, this is the heavy-lift prep phase.

required_inputs.conditional: when shadow box molding in scope

tasks.name: Wipe Dust from Trim Surfaces
tasks.description: Wipe all trim surfaces with tack cloth to remove dust and debris. Essential for proper primer adhesion. Per Fine_Finish_Doctrine Section 15.12.

quality_notes.all: All surfaces wiped clean. No visible dust or debris.

tasks.name: Fill Fastener Holes
tasks.description: Fill nail holes, brad holes, and fastener marks with lightweight spackling. NC trim has high fastener count - approximately 2 holes per 12-16 inches. Per Fine_Finish_Doctrine Section 6.2.

quality_notes.QT3: Fill obvious holes; small pinholes may be left
quality_notes.QT5: Fill every hole, no matter how small

tasks.name: Fill Casing End Grain
tasks.description: Apply wood filler to casing end grain exposures. Typically 2 per door opening, 4 per window opening. Required for bare wood substrates only - factory-primed trim has sealed ends.

quality_notes.QT4: Fill all end grain exposures, smooth finish
quality_notes.QT5: Fill all end grain, perfect smooth finish, invisible after prime

tasks.name: Caulk Trim Joints
tasks.description: Apply paintable acrylic latex caulk to trim-to-wall joints, miter joints, cope joints, and scarf joints. ~72 LF per tube for NC (consistent gaps). Per Materials_and_Consumables_Doctrine.

tasks.name: Sand Trim Surfaces
tasks.description: Sand trim surfaces to create tooth for primer adhesion and smooth filled areas. Grit selection per substrate: 150-180 for factory-primed scuff, 120-150 for bare wood, 220 for MDF faces. Per Fine_Finish_Doctrine Section 15.4, use rigid sanding block for defect leveling.

quality_notes.QT5: Thorough sand 220+ grit, uniform scratch pattern

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Dust wipe -> Fill fasteners -> Fill end grain (if applicable) -> Caulk joints -> Sand. Sand is last prep step before prime to create uniform scratch pattern.

sop_modules.name: Trim Primer Application
sop_modules.description: Primer coat application for trim. Primer selection is SUBSTRATE-DRIVEN per Fine_Finish_Doctrine Section 2.1. Method variants: brush or spray. MDF requires two-step priming (edge seal + face prime).

tasks.name: Spot Prime Knots with Shellac
tasks.description: Apply shellac-based spot primer (BIN or equivalent) to knots, resin pockets, and tannin stains before full primer coat. Blocks stain bleed-through. Per materials.json SYS_KNOT_SPOT_PRIME.

quality_notes.QT4: All visible knots and stains spot primed
quality_notes.QT5: Every knot, stain, and potential bleed source spot primed

tasks.name: Brush Primer on Trim
tasks.description: Apply primer to trim surfaces using brush. Work with grain direction on linear trim. Brush from dry edge back into wet. Per Fine_Finish_Doctrine Section 15.11.1 for trim technique. Primer selection per substrate_condition dimension.

quality_notes.QT3: Complete coverage, even film, no holidays
quality_notes.QT4: Complete coverage, minimal brush marks, even film
quality_notes.QT5: Complete coverage, no visible brush marks, perfectly uniform film

tasks.application_note: Application quality is NOT tiered - drips, sags, and holidays fail at all tiers. Rate varies by QT due to precision and scrutiny differences.

tasks.name: Spray Primer on Trim
tasks.description: Apply primer to trim surfaces via airless spray. Maintain proper distance, 50% overlap, consistent speed. Spray tip selection per trim size: 311 for standard, 413 for tall baseboard/crown. Per materials.json spray tip specifications.

quality_notes.QT3: Complete coverage, even film, no holidays
quality_notes.QT5: Complete coverage, perfect uniformity, no orange peel

tasks.application_note: Application quality is NOT tiered - drips, sags, and holidays fail at all tiers. Rate varies by QT due to precision and scrutiny differences.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: MDF edge seal FIRST (if bare MDF), then spot prime knots (if present), then full primer application. For MDF, faces are primed with latex AFTER edges are sealed with solvent-based product.

sop_modules.name: Trim Prime Cleanup
sop_modules.description: Protection removal and final cleanup after trim priming is complete.

tasks.name: Remove Wall Masking
tasks.description: Remove tape and masking paper from wall surfaces. Remove tape while primer is still slightly tacky for cleanest pull. Required only for spray application.

quality_notes.all: Tape removed cleanly. No paint pull on wall surface.

tasks.name: Remove Fixture Covers
tasks.description: Remove covers from electrical outlets and switches. Required only for spray application.

tasks.name: Remove Floor Protection
tasks.description: Remove drop cloths from work area. Fold toward center to contain debris.

tasks.name: Final Cleanup
tasks.description: Vacuum floor area, clean tools, dispose of consumables. Inspect primed trim for touch-up needs.

quality_notes.all: Work area clean. Tools cleaned and stored. Debris disposed.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Remove wall masking first (spray only), then fixture covers (spray only), then floor protection. Final cleanup is last step. In NC sequence, floor protection may stay in place for subsequent phases.

round_configurations.name: Trim Prime Round - Brush Method
round_configurations.description: Single primer coat for trim using brush application. NC production standard.
round_configurations.notes: Brush is NC production standard for trim. No wall masking required. Floor perimeter protection only.

round_configurations.name: Trim Prime Round - Spray Method
round_configurations.description: Single primer coat for trim using spray application. Faster for large volume but requires wall masking.
round_configurations.notes: Spray is faster (4x production rate) but requires wall masking and fixture covers. Best for large volume NC production with unfinished walls.

module_notes.quality_tier_expression: Quality tier controls inspection/repair intensity and scrutiny level, NOT primer selection or application quality. Per Fine_Finish_Doctrine Section 2.3: QT3 = quick glance at 6ft, QT4 = systematic scan at 3ft, QT5 = lighted critical at arm's length.
module_notes.substrate_driven_primer: Primer selection is driven by substrate_condition dimension, NOT quality tier. This is MANDATORY DOCTRINE per Fine_Finish_Doctrine Section 2.1. Each substrate type requires specific primer chemistry.
module_notes.mdf_two_step_process: Bare MDF requires TWO-STEP priming: (1) Solvent-based edge sealer (shellac or oil-based), (2) Latex primer on faces. Edge seal is MANDATORY - water-based primers cause irreversible fiber raise on MDF edges.
module_notes.fjp_stain_blocking: FJP (Finger-Joint Pine) REQUIRES stain-blocking primer. This is non-negotiable. Without stain-blocking, resin bleed-through will appear within weeks/months.
module_notes.application_method_selection: Per Fine_Finish_Doctrine Section 15.1.1: Brush is appropriate for small scope, occupied spaces, punch list. Spray is appropriate for large volume NC production, unoccupied spaces. Both methods must achieve QT standards.
module_notes.nc_sequencing_context: In NC sequence, trim is typically installed AFTER walls are primed but BEFORE walls are finish painted. Trim priming often occurs in same session as door frame finish work.

valid_input_states.notes: NC trim arrives factory-primed (most common) or bare. Remodel scenarios may encounter existing painted trim. Substrate state mapped via substrate_condition dimension.

output_state.notes: All substrate scenarios output field-primed state, ready for finish coats (SF_TRIM_NC_PAINT).

adjacent_state_protection_rules.notes: Unfinished or primed walls need no protection during trim prime (brush method). For spray method, light masking recommended.
Finished walls require protection from primer drips (brush) or overspray (spray). Spray method upgrades to heavy_mask.

applicability_rules.description: MDF edge sealing is MANDATORY when substrate_condition = bare_mdf
Wall masking required for spray application method
End grain fill required for bare wood substrates only
Knot spot priming when bare wood has visible knots or resin

assumptions.value: floor_perimeter for all trim prime work
assumptions.source: Protection_Zones_Reference.md - Commonly Paired Zones by Spec Type
assumptions.note: Trim brush/spray both use floor_perimeter (not floor_full). Trim work has limited drip radius.

assumptions.value: wall_adjacent zone required only for spray method
assumptions.note: Brush method has no overspray. Spray method requires wall_adjacent masking.

critical_constraints.mdf_edge_seal_mandatory: MDF edges MUST receive solvent-based sealer (shellac or oil-based) BEFORE any latex products. Water-based primers cause irreversible fiber raise on MDF edges. This is MANDATORY DOCTRINE per Fine_Finish_Doctrine and materials.json.
critical_constraints.fjp_stain_block_mandatory: FJP (Finger-Joint Pine) MUST receive stain-blocking primer. Without stain-blocking, resin bleed-through will appear as amber/yellow discoloration within weeks/months. This is non-negotiable.
critical_constraints.primer_is_substrate_driven: Primer selection is driven by substrate_condition dimension, NOT quality tier. Per Fine_Finish_Doctrine Section 2.1. Quality tier controls scrutiny and pace, not material selection.
critical_constraints.application_quality_not_tiered: Application quality is the same at all quality tiers. Drips, sags, holidays, and lap marks fail at QT3 just as at QT5. QT controls inspection scrutiny, not application standards.
